title: Autotune: HintEngine for cost hints and compact quant templates
author: Ananya Patel
release_notes: Introduce an automated hint scorer (HintEngine) and a compact quantization template catalog. These deliver conservative batching/cache/quant defaults that reduce token cost for tiered tenants while preserving latency SLOs. No customer-facing API changes. Backward compatible configs added.
description: Motivation: teams continually ask for recommended defaults that balance cost and latency across heterogeneous workloads. Current manual presets are hard to maintain and often conservative or overfit to specific tenants. This PR introduces HintEngine: a small policy/scoring layer that synthesizes unit-econ signals, sample latency distributions, and KV-cache hit heuristics to emit per-tenant 'cost hints' (suggested batch size, cache TTLs, and quant profile families). The PR also adds a compact, audit-friendly 'quant template' catalog (three conservative/balanced/aggressive templates) plus a dry-run simulator that shows estimated unit-econ impact before apply. What changed: 1) runtime/hintengine: new hint engine service (lightweight scoring, deterministic priority tie-breakers, eviction-safe cache of tenant signatures). 2) policy/catalogs: compact_quant_templates.yaml with three vetted profiles and compatibility matrix for common model families. 3) api/cli: `redwoodctl cost-hint apply --dry-run` that outputs estimated token savings and projected p95 latency delta. 4) telemetry: new metrics (hint_score, hint_rationale, simulated_unit_econ) and a small dashboard manifest. 5) e2e tests & integration harness: workload simulator that verifies suggestions do not push p99 > 2x baseline for the conservative template. Design notes: HintEngine is deliberately conservative by default: it prefers cache-first suggestions, enforces model-compatibility checks for quant templates, and annotates each suggestion with a confidence bucket (low/medium/high) plus an estimated cost delta. The compact quant catalog uses quant-aware fallbacks: when a template is incompatible we suggest the nearest compatible profile and add a fallback flag so runtime can gracefully degrade. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scoring functions - [x] Integration tests with warm/cold KV-cache scenarios - [x] Telemetry gated behind feature flag - [x] CLI dry-run implemented - [x] Docs stub for operations (cost-hints.md) Rollout plan: enable HintEngine in canary for 10 tenants for 48h, collect simulated_unit_econ and actual token consumption, then increase gradually. Linked items: ENG-1452 (HintEngine MVP), ENG-1453 (quant templates catalog). Backwards compatibility: config files are additive; no breaking API changes.
